text: A star about 30 million light-years away keeps erupting like a supernova, and surviving. At least 27 bursts between 2012 and 2026. They call it a supernova impostor. Why? Chandra caught it at least 100 times brighter in X-rays than before its outbursts began. The best explanation: a hidden black hole or neutron star, pulling material off it every 113 days. It is the first X-ray detection of this class of erupting star. Next: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, Wednesday, November 18. Follow Downlink Cat for that milestone.
direction: You are a young, nerdy science creator in your early twenties, a little scrawny, filming a vertical video for your followers. Talk like a popular creator on TikTok or YouTube Shorts, not a narrator: conversational, a grin in your voice, genuinely hyped. Hit the hook hard, take a tiny beat before each reveal, punch the key words (supernova, surviving, 27, impostor, 100, hidden, 113, first, Voyager), speed up through setup lines and slow down on the payoff. Energy: high. A little more cat: a playful purr on a few r sounds and a small 'mrr'-like rise on the question line. Still natural, never a meow.
